blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Running an effective planning process is a discipline, not a single event. The monthly meeting is the visible part, but the real work happens in the weeks before. Each team prepares its numbers, checks its assumptions and flags risks before the group sits down together.

At Czarnikow, the process starts with the demand review. The trading desks share their latest forecasts. Then operations checks capacity, freight availability and warehouse stock. Finance adds the cost and margin view. By the time the leadership meets, the picture is clear and the decisions are focused.

The best companies run this process consistently every month. They do not skip it when things are busy. They know that one hour of good planning saves ten hours of firefighting later.

items.q: According to the text, where does the real work of an S&OP process happen?
options: In the weeks before the meeting
items.why: "The monthly meeting is the visible part, but the real work happens in the weeks before."

items.q: In what order do the teams contribute at Czarnikow?
options: Operations, then finance, then the trading desks
Finance, then operations, then the trading desks
The trading desks (demand), then operations, then finance
items.why: "the process starts with the demand review… Then operations checks capacity… Finance adds the cost and margin view."

items.q: What does the phrase "saves ten hours of firefighting later" most likely suggest?
options: Finance handles most of the emergencies
Poor planning leads to reacting to crises later
Firefighting is part of a healthy process
Meetings should always last ten hours
items.why: Inferência: firefighting = apagar incêndios; sem planejamento você gasta muito mais tempo reagindo a crises.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Preparation before the meeting is essential.
A clear picture makes decisions more focused.
When the team is busy, it makes sense to skip the monthly planning.
Demand, supply and finance views should come together.
items.why: Inferência: o texto elogia justamente quem NÃO pula o processo quando está corrido — "They do not skip it when things are busy."

items.q: What does the text imply about a meeting where each team arrives unprepared?
options: It will spend its time discovering numbers instead of deciding
It will decide faster because there is less data
It will be shorter and more efficient
It will still produce focused decisions
items.why: Inferência: se a preparação acontece antes, sem ela a reunião vira coleta de dados — deixa de decidir.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James corrigindo um processo de S&OP quebrado. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let me be honest about what I saw last month. The S&OP meeting generated a lot of heat and almost no decisions. People arrived with different numbers, half of them out of date, and we spent the first hour just agreeing what the actual forecast was.

That is the wrong place to do that work. By the time leadership sits down, the demand view, the capacity check and the finance numbers should already be refreshed and reconciled. The meeting is the decision point, not the data-gathering point.

So here is what changes. Each team prepares upstream. The desks lock their forecast three days before. Operations calculates the capacity implications and brings two scenarios, not a wish. Finance attaches the margin trade-off to each one. Then we pre-align in a short call, so the surprises come out before the room, not inside it.

Do that, and the monthly meeting shrinks to forty minutes of clean choices. Skip it, and we are back to firefighting. I would rather spend one disciplined hour now than lose ten later.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What was wrong with last month's S&OP meeting, according to James?
options: It generated a lot of heat but almost no decisions
It was too short to reach any conclusion
Leadership refused to approve the forecast
items.why: "The S&OP meeting generated a lot of heat and almost no decisions."

items.q: According to James, what should the meeting be?
options: A review of last year's results
The place to agree the forecast
The decision point, not the data-gathering point
items.why: "The meeting is the decision point, not the data-gathering point."

items.q: What does James ask operations to bring to the meeting?
items.why: "Operations calculates the capacity implications and brings two scenarios, not a wish."

items.q: Why does James want a pre-alignment call before the meeting?
options: To cancel the monthly meeting entirely
So finance can approve the budget
So the surprises come out before the room, not inside it
items.why: "we pre-align in a short call, so the surprises come out before the room, not inside it."

items.q: What does James imply by "I would rather spend one disciplined hour now than lose ten later"?
options: Investing time in preparation prevents far greater time lost to crises
Preparation is a cost he is unwilling to pay
Discipline is less important than speed
The meeting should always last exactly one hour
items.why: Inferência: ele troca uma hora de preparo por evitar dez horas de "firefighting" — preparo compensa.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Running an effective planning process is a discipline, not a one-off event." Here, discipline means…
items.why: Discipline = disciplina: uma prática constante e repetida, não um acontecimento isolado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Bring numbers that are ___, not last quarter's figures."
items.why: Refreshed = atualizado; o oposto de dados velhos.

items.q: "Operations must check capacity before we commit to the volume." Capacity here refers to…
options: the ability to produce or handle a given volume
the size of the sales team
the number of meetings per month
items.why: Capacity = capacidade: quanto a operação consegue produzir ou movimentar.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Each forecast has a cost ___; higher service usually means lower margin."
items.why: Trade-off = compromisso/troca: ganhar de um lado custa do outro.

items.q: "Please align these numbers upstream, before the meeting." Upstream means…
options: earlier in the process, before the later steps
items.why: Upstream = a montante: numa etapa anterior do fluxo, antes das seguintes.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de planejamento. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Finance still has to sign off on the volume plan." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new S&OP cycle desk by desk." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Operations pushed back on the freight assumption." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed the actions but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry them to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Let's circle back on the capacity scenario after the demand review." This means we will…
items.why: Circle back = voltar a um assunto mais tarde na conversa ou no processo.
